author: Chippewa Valley Times
title: UW-Stout announces December expos for student game designs, STEMM research, art and design
text:
Ashley DeMuth, CEO | Menomonie Area Chamber of Commerce
Ashley DeMuth, CEO | Menomonie Area Chamber of Commerce
Three upcoming events at the University of Wisconsin-Stout will showcase student work in game design, STEMM fields, and art and design. The university is inviting both media and the public to attend these events on campus.
The Stout Game Expo (SGX) 2025 will take place on Wednesday, December 10, from 6 to 9 p.m. in the Great Hall of the Memorial Student Center. Attendees will have the opportunity to play a variety of games created by students enrolled in UW-Stout’s two game design and development programs. Earlier this year, these undergraduate programs were ranked fifth among similar programs in the Midwest by Princeton Review.
On Thursday, December 11, from 1 to 3 p.m., the Memorial Student Center will host the STEMM Student Expo. This event serves as an end-of-semester showcase for class projects and research conducted by students in UW-Stout’s College of Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics & Management (STEMM). More than 300 students are expected to present over 100 projects spanning a dozen academic disciplines. The expo is organized by students from the Hospitality Convention/Meeting Planning class.
The SOAD Senior Show Fall 2025 is scheduled for Friday, December 12, from 6 to 9 p.m. at the Applied Arts Building at 415 13th Ave. East in Menomonie. Graduating seniors from all disciplines within UW-Stout’s School of Art & Design (SOAD) will display their work throughout Micheels Hall and the Applied Arts building. The exhibition will feature works ranging from video production and graphic design to industrial and product design, interior design, studio art, animation and digital media, fashion design, and more.
For information regarding media accommodations at these events, Tom Giffey in Marketing Communications can be contacted at 715-232-2384 or [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection).
